title: Catch-up Triage
eyebrow: Triage · open issues and pull requests in Ajw2003/AjsClaudeCodeTools, 27 October 2026

short.lead: While you were away, most of the work landed. Of the 42 issues waiting on your review, 34 are already merged into main and running in every session. With 7 older in-progress leftovers, 41 issues only need closing. One feature is built and passing but not merged: restructure steps 3 to 7, which changes how every session starts. Two features are designed but not built: a changelog page in every repo and the attribution guard on GitHub. The steps below are in the order I suggest. Step 3 is the one with real risk to test now; step 6 touches the most repos but is not built yet.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it does, its state and its risk.

41 issues are finished and only need closing
you

14 issues were tested by you and merged: the verify rework (#368 to #371), the proof check fix (#367, #374 to #376) and the 2.68.1 patch (#307 to #311). #303 (the emergency switch-off) was replaced by that patch.

27 more were merged between 14 and 19 October and have run in every session since. No QA pass was ever logged for them. They are the new item visual (#240 to #243), house labels (#274 to #278), the guards audit (#286, #288 to #293), the in-session attribution guard (#315 to #319) and the writing-check loop fixes (#322 to #327).
Pull request #305 (house-rules 2.68.1: switch off the design loop) should close unmerged, because the real 2.68.1 patch (pull request #312) replaced it.

Approve the sweep (the list of issues further down the page), keeping any issue you want to test first.
lock
2 · Prepare
Set two cloud settings before step 3, or every cloud session stops
you
The restructure (step 3) refuses every tool until the agent's name is set. Cloud sessions start in a fresh container, so the plugin reads the name from environment variables.
I checked this session: HOUSE_RULES_AGENT_NAME is not set, so after the merge a cloud session would be locked until the name is saved each time.

The steps are in docs/cloud-session-setup.md on the branch AjsAgent/issue-281-fix. In each cloud environment's settings, add HOUSE_RULES_AGENT_NAME=ajw2003sAgent and HOUSE_RULES_OWNED_BRANCHES=AjsAgent/,claude/. On your PC, the first session after the update asks for both and saves them once.
Add the two variables to each cloud environment you use.
swap
3 · Test and merge
Restructure steps 3 to 7: built, passing, waiting on your QA
you

What it does: settings and identity (#341), safe git (#349), the design loop and pages (#343), writing and evidence rules (#344) and helper agents (#345), all following your five grilling rounds. Parent #381, release #382.

Where it is: the branch AjsAgent/issue-281-fix, house-rules 2.74.0, 34 files changed, and up to date with main. No pull request is open yet. The five per-step branches (issue-341-settings and the rest) are older copies already inside it.

Tested: I ran verify.py on that branch today and it exited 0, with 966 checks passing. tools/verify_tools.py passed all 47 checks. The QA page is docs/plans/2026-10-24-restructure-steps-3-7-qa.html on the branch.
Risk: high. It changes how every session starts, how commits and pull requests are credited, which deletes are allowed and what helper agents report, on every account that installs the plugin.

Merge order: you asked for background work tracking (#396) to ship as a 2.73.x patch, a lower version than this branch's 2.74.0. The CI version check (tools/check_plugin_version_bump.py) refuses any version that is not higher than main's, so tracking must merge first, as 2.73.1 or later (main is already 2.73.0). If this restructure merges first, tracking has to become 2.74.1.
Once step 2 is done, say "open the restructure pull request", test it in a fresh session, then reply "QA passed: restructure steps 3 to 7".
file

State: still needed, because main's version check still tells a session to run claude plugin marketplace update. The branch is 99 commits behind main, conflicts with it, and uses version 2.69.0, which another release has since used.
Risk: medium. It touches the same core file as the restructure, so it is rebased after step 3 merges.
Nothing yet. After step 3 merges I rebase it (replay its changes on top of the latest main), rerun both test suites (verify.py and tools/verify_tools.py) and give you a QA page.
